Everything they presented as business positives are all retail establishments. Food, hair, yoga, coffee. These things look nice and feel good but they will not create a vibrant local economy. It's just not mathematically possible.

If I may explain: Fundamentally, you will still have a massive trade imbalance between what comes into the community and what goes out of the community.

Two simple equations that are the corollaries of each other:

(Goods going into the city via Walmart, Amazon, Sysco, Sunoco, etc.) > (Goods leaving the city. ) ...therefore... (Cash going out of the city via spending at Walmart, Amazon, Sysco, Sunoco, etc.) > (Cash coming into the city.)

With this imbalance, the lady in the video (who made $$ in NY and LA) can now buy a 40,000 sqft building on the cheap. She has external cash (cash not earned locally) so she can leverage the imbalance.

Unless there are an endless string of investors who have (a) made good money outside the city and (b) have a emotional attachment to the city that overrides their better financial judgement ... then this will go nowhere.

Bottom line: the city must attract businesses that earn $$ not from the local economy but from the national and international economies. We always talk about manufacturing. But, this can also be skilled or artistic work. (Engineering design firms, writers and artist, etc.)
